Source and attribution

The archive attributes this English wording to Walden and files it under Transcendentalism. That locator distinguishes the passage from loose internet attributions: readers can return to the named work or section to check translation, surrounding argument, and edition-specific wording.

About Henry David Thoreau

Henry David Thoreau (1817–1862) was an American essayist, naturalist, and political dissenter of the Concord Transcendentalist circle. Walden (1854) recounts deliberate life at Walden Pond; “Civil Disobedience” justifies refusal of unjust tax.

How to read this passage

Across 4 recurring voices here (notably Epictetus and Augustine of Hippo), awakening is framed through Vedanta and Stoicism. Some passages define awakening; others warn how it fails; still others relocate it inside habit, community, or language. This passage enters that discussion through awakening, life.

Concepts in this quote

Awakening
Awakening appears in this archive as a live philosophical concern—not a slogan. These verified English passages show how thinkers treat awakening as a problem of judgment, practice, or explanation.
Life
Philosophy quotes about life ask what makes a life good, meaningful, or worth examining—questions that drive ethics, religion, and everyday decision.
